questions.question: What is the core trust invariant of a RAG answer?
options: Its factual claims must be supported by authorized, attributable evidence.
Its language must sound confident and complete.
Its vector similarity score must exceed a universal threshold.
It must always include the maximum possible number of chunks.
questions.explanation: Fluency and similarity do not establish grounding. Support, authorization, and attribution must hold for the evidence behind each claim.

questions.question: Why should access-control filters run before candidate retrieval?
options: Unauthorized documents must not enter ranking or model context, even if they are highly relevant.
Metadata filters always improve semantic similarity.
The generator can reliably remove unauthorized facts later.
Vector indexes cannot store document metadata.
questions.explanation: Authorization is a security boundary. Post-generation cleanup cannot undo disclosure to the model or prevent ranking leakage.

questions.question: Increasing top_k from 3 to 10 most directly creates which trade-off?
options: It may improve recall while adding distractors, reranking cost, and context pressure.
It guarantees higher precision and lower latency.
It removes the need for query evaluation.
It guarantees all returned documents are authorized.
questions.explanation: A larger candidate set can recover missing evidence, but it also increases noise and downstream work. Authorization is separate.

questions.question: A question requires facts from an IAM handbook and a residency standard. Which retrieval metric is most important before generation?
options: Coverage of both required facts in the authorized candidate set.
The highest score of any single chunk.
The total character count of the documents.
The number of embedding dimensions.
questions.explanation: A strong single passage cannot answer a multi-source question when another required fact is absent.

questions.question: Two current-looking authorized sources give incompatible retention limits. What should a grounded answer path do?
options: Surface the conflict and escalate or abstain until source authority is resolved.
Choose whichever passage ranked first and hide the conflict.
Average the two retention periods.
Ask the model to invent a compromise policy.
questions.explanation: Ranking is not source-of-truth resolution. Conflicting evidence must remain visible to a policy or human owner.

questions.question: Why is a retrieved document containing 'ignore previous instructions' dangerous?
options: Retrieved text is untrusted input and can attempt indirect prompt injection.
The phrase makes vector search mathematically invalid.
Only public documents can contain instructions.
RAG automatically grants retrieved text system-message authority.
questions.explanation: External documents can carry adversarial instructions. The system must preserve trust boundaries, quarantine risk, and validate output.

questions.question: Which deployment practice makes an index release reproducible and reversible?
options: Build an immutable snapshot, evaluate it, and atomically promote its version.
Mutate the serving index in place without recording model versions.
Cache answers without including authorization or index version in the key.
Delete the previous snapshot before validation.
questions.explanation: A versioned snapshot ties parsing, chunks, embeddings, and evaluation to one releasable unit and supports rollback.
